termsP1: Policy Bias is free software that encodes published party policy. It is not a party, a campaign, or advice about how to vote.
termsP2: The code is MIT. Party policy text, images, PDFs, and logos remain with those parties. We show them so you can tell whose policy it is. That does not give you those rights.
termsP3: The cards are our reading of what the parties published. They can be wrong. Use the source on each card.
termsP4: Playing the game is optional. A submitted score is public. Privacy says what that contains.
termsP5: The software is provided as is, without warranty.
privacyP1: We do not run accounts. We do not collect a name, email, or login.
privacyP2: This browser may keep a lifetime score and a language choice in local storage. That stays on your device.
privacyP3: If you finish a game, you can add an anonymous row to a public dataset: the score, each guess, the calendar day, and optional questions (age band, ethnicity, intended vote, felt wealth). We do not store a cookie, IP address, or user agent with that row. Anyone can read the dataset.
privacyP4: Vercel hosts the site and counts visits without cookies. Ordinary web requests still reach the host.
scoresLede: Anonymous session scores for this event. Each party column is how often that party was guessed, and how many of those guesses were right. Compare that with intended vote. No accounts, names, cookies, or IP addresses.
